Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s).

**Statements:**

Some pencils are rods.

No rod is a door.

All balls are rods.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some pencils being balls is a possibility.

II. No ball is a door.

III. All rods are balls.

IV. No pencil is a door.

options.text: Only Conclusions I, II and IV follow
Only Conclusions I and II follow
Only Conclusions II and III follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/62072659bedbe6b9bdcb0e0e6b7eb70f42310348dd22a3b38124c35637904b5e.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some pencils being balls is a possibility → Follow (As some pencils are rods and all balls are rods. So, as no direct negative or cross relation is given between pencils and balls therefore it is definitely possible)

II. No ball is a door → Follow (As all balls are rods and no rod is a door. So, a direct negative or cross relation is given between door and rod in which whole balls comes in therefore it is definitely true)

III. All rods are balls → Does not follow (As all balls are rods and no rod is a door. So, a direct negative or cross relation is given between door and rod in which whole balls comes in therefore it is definitely false)

IV. No pencil is a door → Does not follow (As some pencils are rods and no rod is a door. So, as no direct negative or cross relation is given between pencils and door therefore it is definitely false)

∴ Here, Only conclusions I and II follow.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Only conclusions I and II follow"

• It is an interface between the computer, user, and the hardware

• Enable user to create and edit text files

questions.question: Which process in bacteria and protozoa results in the splitting of a single cell into two or more daughter cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Binary fission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Binary fission** is a primary method of **asexual reproduction** observed in **unicellular organisms** like **bacteria** and **protozoa**, where a single parent cell divides into **two** approximately equal-sized **daughter cells**. *Hence, this option is correct.*
 
• In **bacteria**, the process begins with the replication of the **circular DNA**, followed by the elongation of the cell and the formation of a **septum** that eventually splits the cell into **two identical individuals**.
 
• **Protozoa** exhibit different patterns of fission; for instance, **Amoeba** can undergo division in any **plane**, whereas **Leishmania** (the causative agent of **Kala-azar**) undergoes fission in a specific **longitudinal orientation** relative to its **flagellum**.
 
• The process is highly efficient and allows for **rapid population growth** under favorable environmental conditions, with some bacteria capable of dividing every **20 minutes**.
 
• Unlike sexual reproduction, **binary fission** does not involve the **fusion of gametes** or the shuffling of genetic material, ensuring that offspring are **genetically identical** to the parent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Budding**:

 
 
• This is an **asexual** process where a new organism develops from an outgrowth or **bud** due to cell division at one particular site.
 
• Common examples include **Yeast** (a fungus) and **Hydra** (an animal). In **Hydra**, the bud uses **regenerative cells** to grow and eventually detaches as a **independent individual**. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Fertilisation**:
 
 
• It is a fundamental process in **sexual reproduction** involving the **fusion** of a **haploid male gamete** (sperm) and a **haploid female gamete** (ovum).
 
• This process results in the formation of a **diploid zygote**, ensuring **genetic variation** in the offspring. It occurs in most **multicellular organisms**, including humans and higher plants. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Pollination**:
 
 
• This is the act of transferring **pollen grains** from the male **anther** of a flower to the female **stigma**.
 
• It is a specific **mechanism** used by **angiosperms** (flowering plants) and **gymnosperms** to facilitate fertilization. It can be **self-pollination** or **cross-pollination** via agents like **wind, water, or insects**. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Multiple Fission**:
 
 
• Apart from binary fission, some protozoa like **Plasmodium** (the **malarial parasite**) undergo **multiple fission**, where the nucleus divides many times to produce **many daughter cells** simultaneously within a **cyst**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison of Fission types**: While **Binary fission** results in **2** daughter cells, **Multiple fission** can produce **hundreds** of progeny, which is an adaptation for survival in **unfavorable conditions** or parasitic lifecycles.
 
• **Genetic Stability**: Because **Binary fission** relies on **mitosis** (or a similar prokaryotic process called **amitosis**), the **DNA** is copied exactly, maintaining **genetic stability** across generations unless **mutations** occur.
 
• **Medical Significance**: Understanding fission is crucial in **Microbiology** and **Medicine**, as many **antibiotics** (like **Penicillin**) work by interfering with the **cell wall synthesis** during the division process of **pathogenic bacteria**.

questions.question: Which folk instrument is made from a dried gourd and played by snake charmers (Kalbeliyas)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pungi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pungi**, also known as the **Been**, is a traditional wind instrument primarily used by **snake charmers** in **India**, particularly the **Kalbeliya** community of **Rajasthan**.
 
• It is constructed using a **dried bottle gourd** (calabash) which serves as the air reservoir and resonator. This gourd is hollowed out to allow air to pass through to the pipes. *Hence, the statement regarding its composition from a dried gourd is correct.*
 
• The instrument typically consists of **two bamboo pipes** inserted into the lower end of the gourd. One pipe, known as the **Jivala**, has finger holes to play the melody, while the other pipe provides a constant **drone** sound.
 
• It is played using a technique called **circular breathing**, where the player inhales through the nose while simultaneously pushing air out from the mouth into the instrument to maintain a continuous, uninterrupted sound.
 
• The **Pungi** is the central musical element of the **Kalbeliya folk dance**, where the movements of the dancers often mimic the fluid, swaying motions of a **cobra**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Kalbeliya Tribe and Dance:**

 
 
• The **Kalbeliya** are a nomadic tribe traditionally known as **snake charmers** and catchers. Their dance form was recognized by **UNESCO** and included in the **Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity** in the year **2010**.
 
• Apart from the **Pungi**, they use other instruments like the **Dufli**, **Khanjari**, and **Dholak** to create rhythmic accompaniment for their high-energy performances.
 
 
 
• **Khanjari:**
 
 
• The **Khanjari** is a **percussion instrument** similar to a small **tambourine**. It consists of a circular wooden frame covered with a single **drumhead** made of **goat skin**.
 
• It is widely used in **devotional music** (Bhajans) and folk songs across **India**. Unlike the Pungi, it does not use a gourd and is not a wind instrument.
 
 
 
• **Morchang:**
 
 
• The **Morchang** is a **jaw harp** or mouth harp made of **iron** or **brass**. It is categorized as an **idiophone**.
 
• The player places the instrument between their teeth and plucks a metal tongue with their finger while using the **mouth cavity** as a resonator to change the pitch and timbre. It is a popular rhythmic instrument in **Rajasthani folk music** and **Carnatic music** (where it is called Morsing).
 
 
 
• **Kamayacha:**
 
 
• The **Kamayacha** is a sophisticated **bowed string instrument** unique to the **Manganiyar** community of **Western Rajasthan**.
 
• It is carved from a single piece of **mango wood** and features a large circular resonator covered with **parchment** (goat skin). It typically has **three main strings** made of **gut** and several **sympathetic strings** made of steel, producing a deep, haunting melody.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Pungi** was famously banned by **Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb** in the royal residence because of its shrill and unpleasant sound. This ban reportedly led to the evolution of the **Shehnai**, which was an improved version of the Pungi.
 
• In **snake charming**, the snake does not actually "hear" the music (as snakes lack external ears) but reacts to the **vibrations** and the **visual movement** of the instrument.
 
• The **Pungi** remains an iconic symbol of **Indian folk music**, though its use has declined in urban areas due to strict **wildlife protection laws** (such as the **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972**) that prohibit the catching and keeping of snakes.

questions.question: The "Chhadi Dance" is associated with the worship of which folk deity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gugga Peer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Chhadi Dance** is a prominent folk dance performed in the **North Indian** states of **Haryana** and **Rajasthan**, specifically during the festival of **Gugga Naumami**. ***Hence, the option Gugga Peer is correct.***
 
• This dance is a ritualistic performance dedicated to **Gugga Peer** (also known as **Goga Ji**), a legendary **snake-god** and warrior-hero who is believed to protect his devotees from **snake bites** and other calamities.
 
• The central element of the dance is the **Chhadi**, a long **bamboo pole** that is decorated with **peacock feathers**, **colorful rags**, **garlands**, and **metal bells**, signifying the spiritual authority of the deity.
 
• The performance usually takes place in the **Hindu month of Bhadrapada** (typically **August** or **September**), on the **ninth day** of the dark fortnight (**Krishna Paksha**).
 
• Devotees, known as **Bhagats**, carry the **Chhadi** from village to village while singing **Gugga Gatha** (ballads) and dancing to the beats of **Deru** (a small wooden drum) and **Manjiras**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Baba Ramdev**:

 
 
• **Baba Ramdev** (or **Ramdevji**) is a revered folk deity of **Rajasthan**, born in the **14th century**. He was a **Tanwar Rajput** ruler who is worshipped as an incarnation of **Lord Krishna**.
 
• He is known for his work toward **social equality** and the upliftment of the **downtrodden**. His main temple is located at **Ramdevra** in **Jaisalmer**.
 
• While he has a huge following and a major fair (**Ramdevra Mela**), the **Chhadi Dance** is specifically not associated with him. ***Hence, the statement is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Sheetla Mata**:
 
 
• **Sheetla Mata** is a **Hindu Goddess** worshipped as the protector against **smallpox**, **measles**, and other heat-related diseases.
 
• Her most famous shrine is the **Sheetla Mata Mandir** in **Gurugram**, **Haryana**. She is traditionally depicted holding a **broom** and a **pot of cool water** while riding a **donkey**.
 
• Devotees visit her shrine during **Sheetla Ashtami**, but her worship does not involve the ritualistic **Chhadi Dance**. ***Hence, the statement is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Sanjhi Devi**:
 
 
• **Sanjhi Devi** is a folk deity worshipped primarily by **unmarried girls** during the **Navratri** period before **Dussehra**.
 
• The ritual involves creating **artistic images** of the goddess on **mud walls** using **cow dung**, **clay**, and **colors** to seek blessings for a **good husband** and **family prosperity**.
 
• This is a form of **folk art** and localized worship and is entirely distinct from the martial and ritualistic **Chhadi Dance**. ***Hence, the statement is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gugga Peer's Heritage**: He was a **Chauhan Rajput** king who lived in the **11th century** in the **Dadrewa** region of **Rajasthan**. He is one of the **"Panj Pirs"** (Five Peers) of the desert region and is worshipped by both **Hindus** and **Muslims**.
 
• **Gogamedi**: This is the site of the largest annual fair dedicated to him, located in the **Hanumangarh** district of **Rajasthan**. It is believed that **Gugga Ji** took **Samadhi** (voluntary burial) at this spot.
 
• **Iconography**: In folk art and the **Chhadi Dance**, the **Chhadi** represents the **Naga** (snake) and the power of the Peer. The **blue horse** is also a common symbol associated with his legends.
 
• **Cultural Impact**: The **Chhadi Dance** serves as a medium for **community bonding** and preservation of **oral history** through the singing of **Vanshavali** (genealogy) and heroic deeds of **Goga Ji**.

Reason (R): It reacts with CO₂ from the air to release Chlorine gas.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) explains (A).

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) explains (A)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Assertion (A)** states that **Bleaching powder** loses its power if kept in the open for a long time. This occurs because the active component responsible for its bleaching action, which is **Chlorine**, is gradually released into the atmosphere, leaving behind an inactive residue. ***Hence, statement (A) is correct.***
 
• **Reason (R)** explains the chemical process behind this loss of power. When **Bleaching powder** (**CaOCl₂**) is exposed to the atmosphere, it reacts with the **Carbon Dioxide** (**CO₂**) present in the air. This chemical reaction results in the formation of **Calcium Carbonate** (**CaCO₃**) and the evolution of **Chlorine gas** (**Cl₂**). ***Hence, statement (R) is correct.***
 
• The "power" of bleaching powder refers to its **oxidizing** and **bleaching capacity**, which is directly proportional to the amount of **available chlorine** it contains.
 
• Since the reaction with **Carbon Dioxide** causes the **available chlorine** to escape as a gas, the remaining powder is no longer effective for bleaching or disinfection. Thus, the reason provided (reaction with CO₂) directly explains why the assertion (loss of power) happens.
 
• The chemical equation for this process is: **CaOCl₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃ + Cl₂↑**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chemical Identity**: **Bleaching powder** is chemically known as **Calcium Oxychloride** or **Calcium Hypochlorite**, represented by the formula **CaOCl₂**. It is a pale yellowish-white powder with a strong smell of **chlorine**.
 
• **Manufacturing Process**: It is produced by the action of **Chlorine gas** on **dry slaked lime** [**Ca(OH)₂**]. This process is typically carried out in a **Hasenclever plant** or a **Bachmann plant**.
 
• **Historical Context**: It was first produced in **1799** by **Charles Tennant** in Glasgow, Scotland, which revolutionized the **textile industry** by significantly reducing the time required for bleaching fabrics.
 
• **Primary Uses**:
 
 
• In the **textile industry** for bleaching **cotton** and **linen**.
 
• In the **paper industry** for bleaching **wood pulp**.
 
• In **water treatment** plants as a **disinfectant** to make drinking water free from **germs** and **bacteria**.
 
• As an **oxidizing agent** in many chemical industries.
 
• For the manufacture of **chloroform** (**CHCl₃**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Storage Guidelines**: Because it reacts with **moisture** and **Carbon Dioxide**, bleaching powder must be stored in **air-tight containers** and kept in a **cool, dry place** away from **sunlight** to prevent decomposition.
 
• **Reaction with Acids**: **Bleaching powder** reacts with dilute acids (like **HCl** or **H₂SO₄**) to release a large amount of **Chlorine gas**. For example: **CaOCl₂ + H₂SO₄ → CaSO₄ + H₂O + Cl₂**.
 
• **Available Chlorine**: A good quality sample of bleaching powder usually contains **35% to 38%** of **available chlorine**. The effectiveness of the powder is always measured by this percentage.
 
• **Safety**: Inhalation of the **Chlorine gas** released from the powder can be irritating to the **respiratory system**, and the powder itself is **corrosive** to the skin and eyes.

questions.question: On rainy days, thin films of oil floating on the water's surface display brilliant colors. this is due to
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is - __Interference__**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Thin-Film Interference__**

 __
 
• The brilliant colors seen in oil films on water are a result of **interference__** of light waves.
 
• When light hits the oil film, some of it reflects off the **__upper surface__** and some reflects off the **__lower surface__** (the interface between oil and water).
 
• The two reflected waves travel different distances; this difference is known as the **__optical path difference__**.
 
• When these reflected waves meet, they undergo **__superposition__**. If they are in phase, **__constructive interference__** occurs, enhancing specific colors.
 
• If they are out of phase, **__destructive interference__** occurs, causing certain colors to disappear.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__ **

__
 
• **Diffraction__**

 __
 
• This is the **bending of light__** waves around the edges of an obstacle or through a narrow opening.
 
• It is responsible for the "fuzziness" of shadows but is not the primary cause of the rainbow-like patterns in oil films.
 
 
 
• **__Polarization__**
 __
 
• This process involves restricting the **vibrations of light__** waves to a single plane.
 
• While **__polarized light__** can be used to analyze stress in materials, it does not create the colors seen in oil slicks through reflection alone.
 
 
 
• **__Factors affecting Interference Colors__**
 __
 
• **Film Thickness__**: Different thicknesses of the oil layer result in different colors being amplified because the path difference changes.
 
• **__Angle of Incidence__**: The color observed changes depending on the **__viewing angle__** because the path the light takes through the film varies.
 
• **__Refractive Index__**: The ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to its speed in the medium (oil) determines how much the light bends and shifts phase.

questions.question: Which of the following will be included in National Income but excluded from GDP at market price?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Net factor income from abroad'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Net factor income from abroad (NFIA):**
 
 
• NFIA refers to the difference between the income earned by residents of a country from abroad (e.g., salaries, wages, profits, or dividends) and the income earned by non-residents within the country.
 
• National Income includes NFIA as it represents the total income earned by a country's citizens, regardless of whether it is earned domestically or internationally.
 
• Gross Domestic Product (GDP) at market price, on the other hand, measures the value of goods and services produced within a country’s geographical boundaries, excluding NFIA.
 
• Thus, NFIA is added to GDP to calculate National Income (commonly represented as GNP or NNP).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indirect taxes:**
 
 
• Indirect taxes, such as GST, VAT, or excise duty, are included in GDP at market price but are excluded from National Income because they do not represent income earned by factors of production.
 
• They are classified as part of market prices, not actual earnings of the country's citizens.
 
 
 
• **Depreciation:**
 
 
• Depreciation refers to the wear and tear or reduction in value of physical assets over time.
 
• It is deducted from GDP to calculate Net Domestic Product (NDP) and is not considered part of National Income as it does not contribute to income directly.
 
 
 
• **Imputed rent of owner-occupied houses:**
 
 
• The imputed rent of owner-occupied houses is an estimated value of rent that homeowners would earn if they rented out their property.
 
• It is included in both GDP and National Income as it reflects income generated from ownership of property.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• National Income is a broad measure that considers the total income earned by residents of a country, including income from abroad (NFIA).
 
• GDP at market price focuses only on the income generated within the geographical boundaries of a country.
 
• To calculate National Income from GDP, adjustments are made for NFIA, depreciation, subsidies, and indirect taxes.

Simple interest for 1 year = 2400 ÷ 2 = Rs. 1200

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years = 2544 − 2400 = Rs. 144

This difference is the interest generated on the first year's SI.

Rate (R) = (144 ÷ 1200) × 100 = 12%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI) for 2 years = Rs. 2400

Compound Interest (CI) for 2 years = Rs. 2544

Time (T) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

For 2 years, Difference (CI − SI) = P × (R ÷ 100)²

⇒ 2400 = (P × R × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ P × R = 120000 --- (Equation 1)

⇒ Difference between CI and SI for 2 years = P × (R ÷ 100)²

⇒ 2544 − 2400 = P × (R² ÷ 10000)

⇒ 144 = (P × R × R) ÷ 10000

⇒ Substitute the value of P × R from Equation 1:

⇒ 144 = (120000 × R) ÷ 10000

⇒ 144 = 12 × R

⇒ R = 12%

⇒ Substitute R = 12 in Equation 1:

⇒ P × 12 = 120000

⇒ P = 10000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 10000.**

CI vs SI for 2 years

The difference between compound interest and simple interest for exactly two years is calculated using the formula: Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)².

CI vs SI for 3 years

Divide the entire equation by 6 ⇒ ∠A/3 = ∠B/2 = ∠C/1.

 A (90°)

⇒ ∠B = x ÷ 3

questions.question: Excluding the stoppages, the speed of a truck is 90 km/h and including the stoppages, the speed of the truck is 36 km/h in a journey. For how many minutes does the truck stop per hour?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Stoppage time per hour = [(Speed without stoppage − Speed with stoppage) ÷ Speed without stoppage] × 60

⇒ Time = [(90 − 36) ÷ 90] × 60

⇒ Time = (54 ÷ 90) × 60

⇒ Time = 36 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 36 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of the truck without stoppages = 90 km/h

Speed of the truck with stoppages = 36 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a930341d3e314e9d5694a0880ce163c5f393fbd22693ce58d82a676ac5211d4d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance covered in 1 hour without stoppage = 90 km

⇒ Distance covered in 1 hour with stoppage = 36 km

⇒ Distance not covered due to stoppage = 90 − 36 = 54 km

⇒ The stoppage time is equal to the time required to cover this 54 km at the original speed without stoppage.

⇒ Time stopped = (54 ÷ 90) hours

⇒ Time stopped = (54 ÷ 90) × 60 minutes

⇒ Time stopped = 3 × 12 = 36 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 36 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Stoppage Time Formula

Stoppage time per hour = (Faster Speed − Slower Speed) ÷ Faster Speed × 60 minutes.

Average Speed

Average speed is the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken. If a journey is divided into two equal parts traveled at speeds a and b, Average Speed = (2 × a × b) ÷ (a + b).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction at speeds a and b (a > b), their relative speed is (a − b). When moving in opposite directions, it is (a + b).
</p

questions.question: The value of an Apple laptop depreciated from Rs. 1,33,100 to Rs. 72,900 in 3 years. Find the yearly rate of depreciation. (Correct to 2 decimal places.)

Ratio of Final Value to Initial Value = 72900 ÷ 133100 = 729 ÷ 1331

For a period of 3 years, take the cube root of the ratio: ³√(729) ÷ ³√(1331) = 9 ÷ 11

This means the value of the laptop drops from 11 parts to 9 parts in one year.

Yearly Depreciation % = [(11 − 9) ÷ 11] × 100 = (2 ÷ 11) × 100

Depreciation % = 18.18%

**∴ The correct answer is 18.18%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Value (P) = Rs. 1,33,100

Final Value (A) = Rs. 72,900

Time (n) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

A = P × (1 − R/100)ⁿ

**Calculations:**

⇒ 72900 = 133100 × (1 − R/100)³

⇒ 72900 ÷ 133100 = (1 − R/100)³

⇒ 729 ÷ 1331 = (1 − R/100)³

⇒ (9 ÷ 11)³ = (1 − R/100)³

⇒ 9 ÷ 11 = 1 − R/100

⇒ R/100 = 1 − (9 ÷ 11)

⇒ R/100 = 2 ÷ 11

⇒ R = 200 ÷ 11

⇒ R = 18.1818... ≈ 18.18%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Depreciation Formula

Depreciation represents a consistent percentage decrease over time and follows the compound interest formula with a negative rate: A = P(1 − R/100)ⁿ.

Appreciation Formula

When an asset's value increases annually (like population growth), use the standard compound interest formula: A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ.

Effective Rate of Successive Depreciation

For two consecutive years with the same depreciation rate R, the net effective depreciation percentage is given by: 2R − R²/100.
</p

questions.question: A rectangular sports field has dimensions (150 m × 120 m). Its length is increased by 0.8% and width is reduced by 0.5%. What is the percent change in the area of the field?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The net percentage change in area of any 2D shape can be found directly using the successive percentage formula without needing its actual dimensions:

Net % Change = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100

Here, a = +0.8 (increase in length) and b = −0.5 (decrease in width).

⇒ Net % Change = 0.8 − 0.5 + (0.8 × −0.5) ÷ 100

⇒ Net % Change = 0.3 − 0.004 = 0.296% ≈ 0.3%

**∴ The correct answer is ~0.3%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial length = 150 m, Initial width = 120 m

Length is increased by 0.8%, Width is reduced by 0.5%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4a533d1aac0e6956ec15156a93ce1c3704fcb0d3034e1bedd7ac557a5b218c63.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial Area = 150 × 120 = 18000 m²

⇒ New Length = 150 + (0.8 ÷ 100 × 150) = 150 + 1.2 = 151.2 m

⇒ New Width = 120 − (0.5 ÷ 100 × 120) = 120 − 0.6 = 119.4 m

⇒ New Area = 151.2 × 119.4 = 18053.28 m²

⇒ Change in Area = 18053.28 − 18000 = 53.28 m²

⇒ Percentage Change = (Change in Area ÷ Initial Area) × 100

⇒ Percentage Change = (53.28 ÷ 18000) × 100

⇒ Percentage Change = 0.296% ≈ 0.3%

**∴ The correct answer is ~0.3%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change Formula

When a final value relies on the product of two variables changing by a% and b% respectively, the net percentage change is: Net Change = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100. For an increase, take the value as positive, and for a decrease, take it as negative.

Approximation Rule for Small Changes

If the individual percentage changes are extremely small (generally less than 2%), the product term (a × b) ÷ 100 becomes practically negligible. The overall net change can be well-approximated simply as the direct sum: a + b.
</p

Weight ratio (Actual : Claimed) = 800 : 1000 = 4 : 5

Profit % = (7 ÷ 8) × 100 = 87.5%

⇒ Actual Selling price = Rs. 30

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer sells goods using false weights, the actual cost price is based on the true weight delivered to the customer, while the selling price is based on the claimed weight.

Successive Ratio Method

The overall profit ratio can be derived by multiplying the individual price markup ratio (CP : SP) by the cheating weight ratio (Actual Weight : Claimed Weight).

questions.question: The angle of elevation of a ladder standing diagonally against a wall is 60° and its lower end is at a distance of 3.7 meter from the wall. Find the length of the ladder.

questions.question: In an election, candidate A got 65% of total valid votes. 25% of total votes were declared invalid. Find the total number of valid votes polled in favour of candidate A, if total numbers of votes are 46000.

**∴ The correct answer is 22,425 votes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total numbers of votes = 46,000

Invalid votes = 25%

Votes in favour of candidate A = 65% of valid votes

**Formula Used:**

Valid votes = Total votes × (100 − Invalid %) ÷ 100

Votes for Candidate A = Valid votes × (A's share % ÷ 100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1c1fd872f70fbd865f30b2281102ee0f4768f2881517bd1d2747a7c3e73075ec.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Valid votes = 75% of 46,000 = (75 ÷ 100) × 46,000 = 34,500

⇒ Candidate A's votes = 65% of Valid votes

⇒ Candidate A's votes = (65 ÷ 100) × 34,500

⇒ Candidate A's votes = 65 × 345 = 22,425

**∴ The correct answer is 22,425 votes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Election Base Concept

In any election problem, percentages are calculated sequentially. Total enrolled voters form the base (100%). Out of these, polled votes are counted. Among polled votes, valid votes become the new base (100%) for calculating the final share of each candidate.

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is subjected to multiple percentage splits (e.g., deducting invalid votes and then finding a candidate's share), you can calculate the result directly using continuous multiplication: Final Value = Initial Base × (1 − Invalid %) × (Candidate %).

Margin of Victory

The winning margin is determined solely by the difference in valid votes secured by the candidates. If Candidate A gets 65% of valid votes, Candidate B gets the remaining 35%. The victory margin would simply be 65% − 35% = 30% of the total valid votes.

questions.question: If 7 times a number exceeds 5over7th of the same number by 176, then the half of the number is :

Half of the number = 28 ÷ 2 = 14.

questions.question: If Radha starts from A with a speed of 30 km/h and Shyam starts from B with a speed of x km/h they meet at C. After the meeting, they reach each other's starting point in 4 hours and 9 hours respectively. Find the speed of Shyam.

Speed Ratio (S₁ ÷ S₂) = √(T₂ ÷ T₁)

⇒ 30 ÷ x = √(9 ÷ 4)

⇒ 30 ÷ x = 3 ÷ 2

⇒ 3x = 60 ⇒ x = 20 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 20 km/h.**

**Formula Used:**

**Calculation:**

By cross-multiplying:

Relative Speed in Opposite Directions

When two objects move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: SRₑₗₐₜᵢvₑ = S₁ + S₂.

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their speeds: SRₑₗₐₜᵢvₑ = |S₁ − S₂|.

Average Speed

If an object covers two equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed for the whole journey is (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

questions.question: If the LCM of two numbers a and b is 60 and their HCF is 15. Determine their mean proportion.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The product of two numbers is equal to the product of their LCM and HCF.

Product = 60 × 15 = 900

Mean proportion of two numbers is the square root of their product.

Mean proportion = √900 = 30

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

LCM of a and b = 60

HCF of a and b = 15

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/43a908ea2dc7e88b431deb67ade97f86de828182f291f2df087497ee9065b396.png]

Product of two numbers (a × b) = LCM × HCF

⇒ a × b = 900

⇒ Mean Proportion = √(a × b)

⇒ Mean Proportion = √900

⇒ Mean Proportion = 30

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**

**__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportion

The mean proportion between two numbers a and b is given by √(a × b).

Third Proportion

The third proportion of two numbers a and b is a value c such that a : b = b : c, which gives c = b² ÷ a.

Fourth Proportion

The fourth proportion of three numbers a, b, and c is a value d such that a : b = c : d, which gives d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Product Rule of Numbers

The guide said to the trekkers, "You must not drink the water from the stream as it might have been contaminated."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. **The guide said to the trekkers,** "Do not drink the water from the stream; it may be contaminated." .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• Option 1 correctly conveys the warning in direct speech: *"Do not drink the water from the stream; it may be contaminated."*
 
• Option 2 is incorrect because it uses the grammatically incorrect phrase *"might is contaminated."*
 
• Option 3 alters the meaning by introducing *"might have been contaminated,"* which changes the timeframe and introduces unnecessary complexity.
 
• Option 4 is incorrect as it suggests that both Options 1 and 2 are correct, which is not the case due to the grammatical error in Option 2.

Correct sentence: *The guide said to the trekkers, **"Do not drink the water from the stream; it may be contaminated."***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Direct speech quotes the exact words spoken by a person.

• Example: He said that he was going to the market.

• To convert a passive sentence into an **active voice**, identify the subject (who performed the action), the verb, and the object.

• The object is "him" (the person being forced).

__
 
• The given sentence uses the phrase **"Not once did the witness mention"**, which is grammatically correct and emphasizes the absence of the witness mentioning a third party.
 
• The construction uses inversion for emphasis, which is common in formal English, especially with negative adverbs like **"Not once," "Never,"** etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Option 1: **"Not once the witness mentioned"** lacks the auxiliary verb **"did"**, making it grammatically incorrect.
 
• Option 2: **"Never once the witness mentioned"** also lacks the auxiliary verb **"did"** and does not follow proper inversion rules.
 
• Option 3: **"Not once the witness had mentioned"** uses the past perfect tense unnecessarily, as the simple past tense is suitable in this case.

The heavy rain caused the river to __**raise significantly above its**__ usual banks, threatening the nearby residential settlements.

• The verb "rouse" is also incorrect because it refers to awakening or stirring someone from sleep or inactivity, which does not fit the sentence's context.
 
• The verb "rise" is correct here because it is an intransitive verb and does not require an object. It accurately describes the river increasing above its usual banks.
 
• The verb "rose" is the past tense of "rise," but the sentence requires the present tense to describe the ongoing effect of heavy rain.

Correct sentence: *The heavy rain caused the river to **rise significantly above its** usual banks, threatening the nearby residential settlements*.

• **Raise:** Transitive verb that requires an object and means to lift or elevate something. Example: "Raise your hand."
 
• **Rouse:** To awaken or provoke someone. Example: "He roused the crowd with his speech."
 
 
 
• **Grammar Tip:**
 
 
• Ensure the verb aligns with the subject and context. In this case, "rise" correctly describes the river's behavior without requiring an object.
 
• Pay attention to tense when selecting verbs to ensure the sentence conveys the intended meaning.

questions.solution:

• The sentence is meant to express a condition that enabled the government to act, but the structure is incorrect.
 
• The correct structure for the sentence should use inversion because "Only by implementing…" is a restrictive clause that requires the verb to precede the subject.
 
• The corrected phrase should read: "**was the interim government able to secure the emergency bailout package**."

Correct sentence: *Only by implementing a series of drastic austerity measures and restructuring the national debt **was the interim government able to secure the emergency bailout package** from the International Monetary Fund, thereby narrowly avoiding a total collapse of the country’s banking system during the winter crisis.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• In sentences starting with restrictive clauses like "Only by," inversion is required.
 
• The verb precedes the subject to emphasize the restrictive clause.
 
• **Example:** Only by hard work **can you achieve success**.
 
 
 
• **Common Errors:**
 
 
• Failing to invert the subject and verb in restrictive clauses.
 
• Using standard sentence structure where inversion is required.

questions.question: Which of the following best captures the central thesis of the passage?

options.text: The inevitable return to Westphalian isolationism as a defense against global cyber-terrorism.
The obsolescence of the nation-state as a relevant actor in modern international diplomacy.
The fundamental erosion of traditional territorial sovereignty due to the rise of digital influence and non-state power.
The superiority of algorithmic governance over democratic processes in maintaining global stability.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***A) The erosion of the Westphalian model.***

 
 
• The passage describes the 1648 Westphalian system—centered on territorial borders and state monopoly of force—as becoming **"increasingly anachronistic"** in the digital age. Physical borders are now permeable to the flow of data and subversive influence.
 
 
 
• ***B) The rise of "Infopolitics" and non-state actors.***
 
 
• Power is shifting from the control of physical space (geopolitics) to the control of digital architectures (infopolitics). Global tech conglomerates now wield **"algorithmic sovereignty,"** challenging the state's exclusive right to govern discourse and internal affairs.
 
 
 
• ***C) The decoupling of power from geography.***
 
 
• The author argues that modern threats (like cyber-attacks) and influence (sharp power) do not recognize the **"sanctity of the border,"** forcing the state to transition from a "rigid container of authority" to a "nodal actor" within a global network.
 
 

Therefore, the central thesis is the **fundamental erosion of traditional territorial sovereignty due to the rise of digital influence and non-state power (Option 3).**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**: Incorrect because the author suggests Westphalian isolationism is outdated and states must instead become "nodal actors" in a network, rather than retreating into isolation.
 
• **Option 2**: Incorrect because the passage doesn't claim the state is irrelevant, but rather that it is in a "defensive crouch" and must **reimagine** its role to survive.
 
• **Option 4**: Incorrect because while the author discusses algorithmic governance, they frame it as a "disruption" to the political order rather than an ideal or superior method for stability.

• Because sharp power operates in the "intangible ether" of cyberspace, it renders traditional territorial borders and non-interference policies as "legal fiction," allowing for attacks that are launched from afar with plausible deniability.
